candidate_claims.text: But the historical truth is that even today, India’s per capita carbon emissions are less than half the global average.
On these very subjects, during COP‑21 in Paris, we launched the book Convenient Action – Continuity for Change.

India is the only country in the G20 – I say this before the big leaders of the G20 – the only country that has fulfilled all the commitments it made at the COP‑21 summit in Paris, and has done so ahead of schedule.
This is the strength of Hindustan that I am talking about.
Twelve years ago, India’s solar energy capacity was about 2 gigawatts.

From 2 gigawatts to 160 gigawatts in 12 years.

We have also completed the ambitious One Nation, One Grid project.
From solar energy alone, India has succeeded in preventing nearly 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions.
Friends, Along with solar energy, India has also achieved major accomplishments in other clean energy sectors.
In the past 12 years, the country’s wind energy capacity has tripled.
Hydropower capacity has increased significantly.
A pathway has also been created to bring private players into this sector.
Because of these efforts, today India’s non‑fossil energy capacity has nearly quadrupled.

Wherever semiconductor ecosystems have been built in the world, they have been prepared after decades of effort.
The size of our first phase was about 8 billion dollars, while the second phase we have set at 13.5 billion dollars.
So far, 12 projects have been approved, and in the next phase this scope will expand further.
And as you were told, we have already trained more than 70,000 youth.
Such a large talent pool is nothing less than a gold mine for all of you.
For years, people in your industry talked about transistor size.
In the past two years, the global semiconductor market has grown by more than 20 percent.
And a very big part of this growth is due to demand created by AI.
That means, today if you are working on AI, the challenges are not only about what is inside the chip, but also about what is happening around it.
In the past decade, our installed solar energy capacity has increased from about 2 gigawatts to more than 160 gigawatts – from 2 to 160.
This sector has been opened to private players.
Just a few years ago, our Constitution completed 75 years.
India’s aspirations are before you, and the new opportunities being created in India are ready to welcome you.

As AI expands, the need for computing power will increase at the same pace.

items.title: PM’s address at the BRICS Business Forum 2026

candidate_claims.text: When the group was launched in 2006, it comprised only four countries.
Today, the BRICS countries represent 50% of the world’s population, 40% of global GDP, and more than 25% of global trade.
Not only that, over these years, while global GDP has grown by around 2.5 times, the combined GDP of BRICS countries has grown by around 4.5 times.
In other words, the economic strength of BRICS has grown at nearly twice the pace of the world economy.
The Forum being held in India is the largest-ever BRICS Business Forum.
With more than 200,000 start-ups and over 120 unicorns, India is emerging as a hub for global solutions.
Today, 50% of the world’s real-time payments are powered by this technology.
To build new solutions on this digital layer, we have provided industry and start-ups with an open ecosystem.
Friends, Today, as trade barriers are increasing around the world, India is building economic bridges.
Since 2014, we have entered into Free Trade Agreements with nearly 40 countries around the world.
Therefore, under our Presidency, we have established new cooperation networks in areas such as agriculture, healthcare, skills, and smart grids.
To connect start-ups and SMEs with markets and finance, we have launched initiatives such as the BRICS Incubator Network, BRICS MSME Portal, and BRICS Startup Innovation Fund.

items.title: PM’s address during inauguration of Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai

candidate_claims.text: I am happy that today another hat‑trick has been achieved.
One hat‑trick was in 2024 when the government was formed for the third time, and another hat‑trick is my presence among you.
Bowing to Ganapati Bappa, I extend my best wishes to all of you for Global Fintech Fest 2026.
And even in such a situation, when India grows at 7.8 percent, the world gains new confidence.
This shows how assured the world is about India’s growth momentum, our macro‑economic stability, and the structural reforms carried out in recent years.
I spoke about it last year too.
Friends, Just a few days ago, on 25th August, UPI completed 10 years.
Ten years ago, when I said that your bank would be at your fingertips, some people thought it impossible – and I am talking about well‑informed people, remember their faces.
I am not talking about the millions of Indians whose bank accounts had just been newly opened then.
Friends, Today, in the month of August alone, more than 2,400 crore transactions were done through UPI.
That means, in just the time we have been sitting here, in 10 minutes alone, on average more than 5 million UPI transactions have taken place across the country.
India’s UPI is now live in 11 countries.
Friends, I am completing 25 years in the ecosystem of policy and governance.
And Indians are the largest in the world in sending money back home.
We adopted those standards and rules that others had created.
PM SVANidhi connected millions of street vendors to the formal system.
And studies show that the average annual income of these beneficiaries has increased by more than 20 percent.
That is why the government has decided to extend this scheme until 2030.
Friends, PM SVANidhi would not have achieved this success if UPI did not exist.
Friends, The first quarter of the 21st century has ended.
Now we are in the year 2026.

candidate_promises.text: When one goal is achieved, I immediately begin preparing for an even bigger goal.
Our next goal should be to connect with the payment systems of those countries.
We must move forward with this goal.
I believe the next chapter of fintech will be written here.

items.title: PM’s speech during the ‘Namo for Viksit Bharat’ programme in Vadodara, Gujarat

candidate_claims.text: Governor of Gujarat Acharya Devvrat ji, the popular Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendra Bhai Patel, many distinguished leaders from other states who have joined us online – Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma ji, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ji, Deputy CM Eknath Shinde ji, Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar ji, other ministers, MPs, MLAs, and the lakhs of citizens gathered there.
Just a short while ago, projects worth thousands of crores of rupees connected to the country’s development were inaugurated and foundation stones laid here.
And today I saw, for the past week, every family has created an atmosphere of cleanliness.
Today, the last links of the Dedicated Freight Corridor have also been joined from here.
Today, the project of more than 2,800 kilometers of Dedicated Freight Corridor has been completed.
This is a very historic achievement for 21st‑century India.
Friends, This Dedicated Freight Corridor is proof of how the work culture of the country has changed in the past 12 years.
The idea of this corridor began in 2004.
In 2006, a special company was created to carry out this work, and then until 2014, the files just kept moving from here to there.
And in 2014, the people of Vadodara, Gujarat, and the nation sent me from Gujarat to Delhi.
The earlier government remained until 2014.
The truth was that in seven–eight years – my young friends, listen carefully and remember – in seven–eight years not even one kilometer of the freight corridor was completed.

Friends, After 2014, the education and lessons you had given me here, what this land had taught me, the lessons I carried with me to Delhi – as soon as we reached there, we began to give speed to this project.
Today, the 2,800‑kilometer corridor has been completed.
Today, on the Eastern and Western freight corridors, more than 430 freight trains run every day – 430 freight trains daily.
Earlier, a freight train took six and a half hours to cover 100 kilometers.
Now the same freight train covers 100 kilometers in less than half that time.
Where sending goods by truck normally took 30 hours, on the Dedicated Freight Corridor the same distance is completed in 10–12 hours.
That means, with freight trains running on this corridor, fuel is saved compared to trucks and trains, freight costs are reduced, time is saved, and the environment benefits.
With this train, in one trip, goods equal to more than 250 trucks were transported from Mumbai to Vadodara – 250 trucks.
In Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra – the tribal areas here are also being connected to rail through this project.
In earlier governments, in the budget, one or two trains would be announced, and they would beat drums about it for a whole year.
Whereas today, throughout the year, one new train after another is being launched.

Friends, Roads, railways, metros, airports, gas pipelines, homes for the poor – when these things are built for crores of people in the country, life becomes easier, and at the same time, millions of employment opportunities are created for workers, from small to large.
Take railways alone – this year’s rail budget has been more than 2.75 lakh crore rupees, which is many times higher compared to 12 years ago.

candidate_promises.text: And coaching will be given by India’s best teachers.
Therefore, we must keep the goal of a developed India in 2047 as supreme.
But let us decide once that now we will not allow Vadodara to become dirty again.
Then Diwali will shine brilliantly, Navratri will be celebrated splendidly, Ganeshotsav will be adorned with glory.
